A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SOPHIA research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A-G are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original training and evaluation results across eight multimodal benchmarks, alongside geometry evaluations, ablations, and training-data analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds a manual evaluation of hallucinations and logical inconsistencies in 50 MMMU Pro cases.

M1.justification: The semi-off-policy sampling, reward propagation, shortest-trajectory selection, and policy update remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1. The added caption-representation discussion explains the existing method without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Training datasets, benchmark coverage, and evaluated task domains are retained. The new manual analysis samples existing MMMU Pro questions; it introduces no distinct task, population, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched experiments. New Table 9 reuses the existing InternVL3.0-38B versus SOPHIA comparison, and the QwQ Preview/DeepSeek-R1 comparison already appeared in v1 Table A2.

E3.justification: Section 6.5 introduces manual evaluation of 50 randomly sampled MMMU Pro cases before and after SOPHIA training, reporting proportions with visual hallucinations and logical inconsistencies. Existing benchmark splits, decoding settings, and training configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.5 adds a focused error analysis addressing hallucinations and logical inconsistencies. Existing ablations are retained: the warm-up analysis moves from Appendix D/Table A1 to Section 6.3/Table 6, while the expanded teacher discussion reinterprets an existing comparison.

E5.justification: No new confidence intervals, error bars, seed information, or formal significance tests are reported. The new manual-analysis percentages are point estimates; existing sampling information is unchanged.

E6.justification: New Table 9 reports base/SOPHIA visual-hallucination rates of 38%/16% and logical-inconsistency rates of 54%/44%. Appendix B.3 adds approximate computational-cost results, including 3-4 times slower inference. All pre-existing numerical table results are retained after matching relocated tables.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(7), Appendix A's formal assumptions, and its lemmas and proofs are unchanged. The new caption-sufficiency discussion in Section 4.1 provides conceptual justification without revising the mathematical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions, benchmark-performance claims, and claim that SOPHIA provides better initialization for subsequent on-policy RL. New supporting evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds a rationale for captions preserving reasoning-relevant visual information. Appendix D extends the existing response-style interpretation to teacher strength, and Appendix F explicitly identifies missing low-level pixel and gradient information as a limitation. Section 6.5 interprets its new error results as supporting the visual-understanding motivation.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.3 provides approximate relative training-computation and inference-cost information, including the 3-4 times inference slowdown. These are additional disclosures, not documented changes to training. Existing implementation settings and prompts remain unchanged; hardware and detailed timing procedures remain unspecified.

R1.justification: V2 adds Liao et al.'s Langbridge as reference 57 to support the visual-to-language embedding rationale in Section 4.1. The existing related-work discussion and broader research positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: V2 moves the warm-up discussion into the main ablation section, adds short error-analysis and computational-cost subsections, and expands several explanatory paragraphs. It also adds acknowledgements and updates title capitalization and affiliation ordering. Most prose and the overall organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 9, relocates the warm-up table from appendix Table A1 to main-text Table 6, and enlarges several existing tables and Figure 3. Associated renumbering and page reflow do not represent new results; existing plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: V2 adds direct, limited evidence about error types central to its motivation through Section 6.5/Table 9, while improving computational-cost disclosure, applicability qualifications, and display readability. These gains are constrained by the small manual sample, absent annotation and uncertainty details, and sparse cost-measurement information. The core method and original benchmark findings remain unchanged.
